_about: Shared geography for the Sheppard_Cortes_recruits_the_arrest_army clip (Dwarkesh map style). Prepared by the director 2026-10-01. lon/lat WGS84. Every builder of this clip reads this file; do not edit it, extend it in your own data module.

santiago_de_cuba.note: Velázquez's seat as governor of Cuba (capital 1515-1556)

cabo_san_antonio.note: western tip of Cuba; both fleets left Cuba past it

san_juan_de_ulua.note: Narváez landed here 22 April 1520 (Cortés too, 21 April 1519)

cempoala.note: Totonac city; Narváez's camp; Cortés's night attack 27/28 May 1520

tenochtitlan.note: Mexica capital on Lake Texcoco; Cortés held Moctezuma here; Alvarado left in charge May 1520

narvaez_voyage_1520.note: Velázquez's second expedition under Narváez, sailed 5 March 1520, 19 ships, landed San Juan de Ulúa 22 April 1520. Line starts at Velázquez's seat (Santiago) and follows the south coast of Cuba, the Yucatán coast and the Bay of Campeche (the usual 1518-1520 route; Cortés's 1519 fleet sailed the same way). Waypoints are checked offshore against Natural Earth 10m; smooth them (centripetal Catmull-Rom) and keep the smoothed curve >= 5 km offshore except at the two ends.

cortes_road_1519.note: Cortés's march inland Aug-Nov 1519 (the 'going beyond' of his licence): Cempoala - Xalapa - Xico - Ixhuacán - Zautla (Xocotlan) - Ixtacamaxtitlán - Tlaxcala - Cholula - Paso de Cortés - Amecameca - Ayotzingo - Iztapalapa - Tenochtitlan (8 Nov 1519). He used the same road down to Cempoala in May 1520 and back up with Narváez's men (arrived 24 June 1520). All points checked on land.

aztec_empire_1519.source: Aztec Empire 1519 map-fr.svg (Wikimedia Commons, Keepscases & Sémhur after Yavidaxiu; from Atlas del México prehispánico, Arqueología Mexicana 2000), georeferenced by affine fit to 22 town markers + Natural Earth coastline ICP (coast median 4 km, p80 10 km; towns rms 15 km)
aztec_empire_1519.note: Outer ring and the Soconusco exclave are filled; the two negative-area rings are holes (even-odd). The Metztitlan and Yopitzinco independents are notches in the outer ring. The polygon slightly overshoots the coast in places, so CLIP IT TO NATURAL EARTH LAND before drawing. Cempoala lies inside it (a tributary Totonac city).

lake_texcoco_1519.source: same georeferenced map (the Valley of Mexico lake system, 1519)
lake_texcoco_1519.note: Draw as water in the static map (sea colour, cream coast line). Tenochtitlan sits on its west side.

facts.cortes_1519_fleet: 11 ships, about 500 men (sources 500-550 soldiers + ~100 sailors), 13-16 horses, left Cuba Feb 1519 (Wikipedia Hernán Cortés; Díaz del Castillo)
facts.narvaez_1520_fleet: 19 ships, about 900 men (Wikipedia Battle of Cempoala: ~900 with ~80 horsemen, ~80 musketeers, ~10 guns; other sources 1,100-1,400), sailed 5 March 1520, landed 22 April 1520
facts.battle_of_cempoala: night of 27/28 May 1520; Cortés 266 Spaniards (+ ~200 Chinantec allies) against Narváez's ~900; Narváez lost an eye and was captured; most of his men joined Cortés (allure of Tenochtitlan's riches)
facts.after: Cortés had left ~80-200 men with Alvarado in Tenochtitlan; he marched back with ~1,300 Spaniards and 96 horses plus Tlaxcalan allies (Díaz), arriving 24 June 1520
facts.dot_scale: 1 dot = 10 men: Narváez's force 90 dots, Cortés's force at Cempoala 27 dots, Cortés's 1519 expedition 50 dots
